title: A Single Quote Inside Double Quotes

learning.python:
In Hello World you wrote a string between double quotes: "Hello World!". A single quote, ', can go inside a double-quoted string just as it is:

print("Don't stop.")   # prints: Don't stop.

A double-quoted string ends at its closing ", so a ' inside it is just another character.

You may also see \', a backslash before the quote. Inside double quotes it prints the same ', but it isn't needed there, and it isn't what this question asks for.
